doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: American politics seen from Europe
summary: Reaction in Europe to Trump's second election, nationalism and anxiety.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: This is a question you can pass on if you’d like. As an American living abroad, do you observe the political and social scene in the United States, and how does it strike you?

Everybody that I’ve talked to over here is stunned by the stupidity of half of the American public. They can’t understand how this happened a second time. But everybody is also afraid because a lot of countries here are swinging to the right. Countries are getting more nationalistic because of immigrants and Covid and all the shit that’s happened. So it’s scary. Brexit, LePen almost winning here in France. I don’t remember the name, the prime minister in Italy, but the woman — Sweden has gone a little further to the right, so it’s kind of happening everywhere but none of them can compare to Trump in terms of lack of intelligence and an evil agenda and the shit he’s gotten away with and so I don’t know if that answers your question.

It does and it’s striking that half the country feels like you do and myself and so forth, and not to make a political agenda out of this interview but I was curious, from you know the other side of the ocean what the feeling is.

Yeah everybody is shocked and frankly they’re frightened by what’s going to happen economically because of the tariffs and all this stuff he’s talking about doing, and also what’s doing to happen to Ukraine and the war in Israel. I mean so yeah, everybody’s on heightened alert I would say, and depressed.
Yeah where do we go from here.
